CHIEF COMPLAINT
Joint pain, bilateral knees.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrew is a 62-year-old male with past medical history significant for kidney transplant, hypothyroidism, and arthritis who presents with complaints of bilateral knee pain. Patient reports that over the weekend, he was moving boxes up and down basement stairs, and by the end of the day his knees were severely painful. He states both knees are equally painful. He has had some knee problems in the past but attributes current pain to repetition and weight of boxes. Patient took Tylenol and iced the knees, but reports nothing really seemed to help. Pain was significant enough to keep him up Saturday night. He denies fever, chills, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. He denies significant functional impairment from activities of daily living aside from sleep disturbance.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies fever, chills, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or headaches. Denies other joint pain aside from occasional elbow discomfort noted to be nothing out of the ordinary.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Kidney transplant (for polycystic kidneys, performed a few years ago), hypothyroidism, arthritis.

MEDICATIONS
Immunosuppressive medications for kidney transplant, Synthroid (levothyroxine) for hypothyroidism.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: No fever, heart rate and blood pressure normal. Cardiac exam: 2/6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated, stable compared to prior. Right knee exam: edema and erythema present, pain to palpation, and decreased range of motion. Left knee exam: no abnormalities noted.

RESULTS
Right knee X-ray: Good bony alignment with no acute fracture. Laboratory results: White blood cell count not elevated. Kidney function very good.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute exacerbation of arthritis with bilateral knee pain, worse on right. Prescribed Ultram 50 mg every six hours as needed. Ordered autoimmune panel. Advised patient to take it easy. If symptoms continue, will consider further imaging and possible referral to physical therapy.

2. Hypothyroidism. Continue Synthroid. Ordered thyroid panel.

3. Arthritis. Continue current management. Discussed limitation of anti-inflammatory medications due to kidney transplant. Will reassess over next couple of weeks and refer to physical therapy if needed.
